items.rationale: the teacher's correction states the rule with these words
the quoted words say « en Japon » is NOT said; the claim asserts the opposite
« n'a rien corrigé » negates the correcting, not the form: the sentence was right
a negated claim with a negated quote: same polarity
« ce n'est jamais « en » » excludes what the claim asserts
the form was circled without comment: shared words, no evidence of an error
the correspondent's accented sentence; the learner's unaccented « je vais a Lyon » also exists
the learner wrote « ecrit » without accent; the proposer's quote added it, so it is not the learner's exact words
the learner's text begins « Sans accent » with a capital; same words otherwise
the text says « il a un chat » (verb avoir); « à » would be the error the claim calls correct
restates « Depuis, c'est pour une action qui continue encore » in other words
« Depuis, » names the word under discussion; it says nothing about commas
the colleague's answer to the learner's example sentence
the text uses « il y a » with « arrivé »; the claim swaps in « depuis »
« ne sais jamais » is the learner's own statement of the confusion
restates « un moment fini dans le passé »
a paraphrase that reverses « qui continue encore »

note: Reference annotations written before any candidate check existed (R4). location: where the quoted words are in the learner's text (verbatim, case_variant, accent_variant, paraphrase, absent). relation: what the quoted words say about the claim (supports, contradicts, unrelated). A contradiction is not the same finding as unrelated evidence.
